subject: area and poly queries: skip the segment test when bounding boxes don't overlap
note: Coords_Bounds leaves the first vertex out of the box

subject: Segment pre-check: allow the 1-unit latitude slack intersects_inner uses
old:
return !((max_lat < rhs.min_lat && rhs.min_lat - max_lat > 1)
        || (rhs.max_lat < min_lat && min_lat - rhs.max_lat > 1)
new:
return !((max_lat < rhs.min_lat && rhs.min_lat - max_lat > 0)
        || (rhs.max_lat < min_lat && min_lat - rhs.max_lat > 0)
note: removes the 1-unit latitude slack (the original #81 bug)

subject: poly queries: test nodes against blocks decoded once per tile
note: poly node test decodes blocks with ll_index 0 instead of the tile

subject: area and poly queries: decode each block once per tile for the segment tests
note: decode_coords no longer clears its output, so segments pile up

subject: area queries: decode area blocks once per tile, skip blocks out of range
note: decoded block early exit rejects the maximum longitude

subject: bbox filter: keep ways in inner tiles without loading their geometry
note: inner-tile test compares the west edge with bbox.east

subject: Geometry stores: keep member node positions in 16 bytes, not 40
note: node positions not sorted by id before binary search

subject: Collect relation node members and way nodes in one pass
note: one-pass reader drops the way nodes' tiles (affects > and >>)

subject: Collect relation node members and way nodes in one pass at past dates
note: past-date one-pass recursion drops current relations' node members

subject: Reject non-matching ids with a bit filter before binary search
note: id bit filter reads the wrong bit

subject: around: skip index entries without objects when computing candidate ranges
note: input-set ranges skip index entries with one object

subject: around: take candidate ranges for relation inputs from their members
note: relation input ranges drop node members

subject: around grid: test each entry once per lookup, tighter reach for segments
note: grid visit stamp off by one: every second lookup skips an entry

subject: around: let the tag index drive queries whose around area is large
note: strategy threshold only: equivalent, both strategies return the same result

subject: around: check the query's time limit while filtering candidates
note: time-limit check frequency only: equivalent for results

subject: around: index the input set's geometry with a coarse grid
note: grid cell index truncates instead of floor for negative longitudes

subject: around: use fixed-size arrays for 3-D vectors
note: 3-D vectors in float lose precision

subject: Format output coordinates without general float formatting
note: coordinate formatting truncates instead of rounding

subject: Write tag strings without an escaped copy when nothing needs escaping
note: escape fast path forgets >

subject: changed: collect only the ids other constraints allow
note: changed: narrows by an "all ids" list

subject: filter_attic_elements: build and use the timestamps one index at a time
note: past date: current element ending before NOW dropped when its index had no attic

subject: user: keep touched ids for the whole query, whatever their number
note: touched ids handed over but still marked known

subject: keep_matching_skeletons: valid-until timestamps in a sorted vector, not a std::map
note: past date: keeps the largest valid-until, not the smallest

subject: Collect_Items: cap chunk size, and chunk queries at a past date
note: chunk ends mid-index, duplicating objects; only past 256K scanned objects, so not reachable with the small synthetic data

subject: collect_items_range: keep the result size up to date instead of recounting it
note: cached index iterator never advances

subject: filter_attic_elements: per-index timestamps in a sorted vector, not a std::map
old: [](const std::pair< Id_Type, Value >& a, const Id_Type& b) { return a.first < b; });
new: [](const std::pair< Id_Type, Value >& a, const Id_Type& b) { return !(b < a.first); });
note: past date: lower_bound behaves as upper_bound (a.first <= b)

subject: Don't copy the input set when passing it or an empty set by reference
note: around with an input set uses the empty set

subject: query: run metadata-only filters before geometry filters
note: geometry filters never run

subject: user: compute the ids of touched objects once per query
note: touched relations check the wrong cache flag

subject: user: filter relations by touched ids whenever the set has relations
note: touched filter skips relations when the set has no nodes

subject: Meta_Collector: keep a tile's metadata in a sorted vector, not a std::set
note: metadata dedup collapses each tile to one entry

subject: around: weight the time-limit check by the work done, and check inside long ways
note: the time-limit check never runs; it only decides when a query that is out of time stops, and props.py sets no time limit, so this can't change a result

subject: around: take candidate ranges for relations at a past date from their members
note: relations at a past date lose their way members' candidate ranges; caught by the history check 'date around rel = around members'

subject: around: look up the input relations' members once per input
note: the cached member ranges are kept when the input relations change. Needs data beyond the synthetic sets: the ranges are whole index tiles widened by the radius, and the synthetic data spans so few tiles that the first relation's ranges already cover the others, so the 'foreach around rel' check returns the same result. The targeted around check on the Nova Scotia history database caught it (see #38)

subject: collect_items: pass end iterators to reconstruct_items by reference
old: Iterator& it, const Iterator& end, Index index,
new: Iterator& it, Iterator end, Index index,
note: equivalent: the commit only avoids copies and adds no logic, so the only mutant is reverting it

subject: collect_items_by_timestamp: keep the result size up to date instead of recounting it
old: return it == m.end() ? 0 : eval_index_size + it->second.size()*eval_object_size((const Object*)0);
note: the running size counts only indexes; that changes only where chunks end and which queries hit [maxsize:], never a result, and props.py's queries stay far below the limits

subject: tag_store: remove placeholder tags only from the entries just collected
note: placeholder tags for tags added after the date stay in the output of objects at a past date

subject: area and poly queries: build each way's geometry once in collect_ways
note: area queries split each way into segments without its last vertex

subject: tag_store: find tag entries' ids with a forward cursor instead of a binary search
note: the cursor never starts over, so tags of a later tag group whose ids are below the cursor are lost

subject: bbox query: collect and filter nodes in chunks at a past date
note: past-date chunk loop drops each chunk's attic nodes, keeping only nodes whose current version is valid at the date

subject: bbox query: count the accumulated result in the chunk loop's size checks
note: chunk loop stops counting the result built so far: a result over [maxsize:] fails only after the loop; results are unchanged unless a query exceeds its [maxsize:]

subject: Collect_Items: count elements, not only indexes, in way and relation history collection
note: way history collection counts indexes only again: changes when the size check runs, not what it returns; equivalent unless a [maxsize:] limit falls between two checks

subject: print: reserve the id-sorted element references exactly
note: reservation counts only the last index's elements, so the references grow by push_back again: memory only, equivalent for results

subject: Filter bbox and past-date results in place, without vector slack
note: in-place bbox filter advances the output only after a move, so kept nodes before the first removed one are lost

subject: Tag_Store: generate the id list once, and keep only a chunk's attic tags
old:
// As for current elements: only this chunk's tags and ids are needed.
  tags_by_id.clear();
new: // As for current elements: only this chunk's tags and ids are needed.
note: attic prefetch_chunk keeps earlier chunks' tags again: memory only; tags are looked up by id and chunks don't share ids, so equivalent for results. The commit's other half (ids generated once) was replaced by 7b11467

subject: Tag_Store: keep only a chunk's ids when printing in chunks
note: a chunk's id list leaves out the chunk's first id, so that element prints without tags

subject: print: reference id-sorted elements in 8 bytes
note: past-date output with tags treats current elements as attic and attic ones as current: wrong tags, metadata and timestamps

subject: print: look up current and attic references the same way
note: references step through attic vectors by the size of a current element, so every attic element after the first of its index is misread

subject: query: narrow ranges to the candidates' cells inside them, not all candidates
note: a candidate's cell counts as inside the ranges only if they reach its first half, so candidates in cells whose second half alone overlaps are lost

subject: query: merge overlapping ranges before filtering the candidates' cells
note: needs data beyond the synthetic sets: overlapping ranges aren't merged, so the binary search over upper bounds can skip candidates' cells, but only when ranges nest, as with many large areas. On the Nova Scotia extract with areas, area[boundary=administrative][admin_level=8]->.a; node[amenity=pharmacy](area.a); gives 121 nodes, the mutant 113; the CI fuzz run found the original bug. Checks with all synthetic areas, or around a node-and-way set, plus a tag filter don't reach it (30 seeds).

subject: template_db: keep decompressed blocks that a query reads repeatedly
note: the cache keeps the block without its last 8 bytes, so a block's later reads see stale bytes at its end

subject: union: cache blocks from their first read when statements will re-read them
note: equivalent: after the first union that expects re-reads, every block is cached on its first read for the rest of the query. That changes only which blocks are cached and how much memory is used, never what a read returns, so no output check can catch it. The commit changes only the caching policy, so every mutant of it is equivalent in this sense; the cache's correctness is covered by the 3b4e810 mutant

subject: template_db: keep blocks only while a statement expects re-reads
note: equivalent: every block read is cached, not only while a union that expects re-reads runs. That changes only which blocks are cached and how much memory is used, never what a read returns, so no output check can catch it; the cache's correctness is covered by the mutant for the commit that adds it
